name: Musée du Petit Palais
notes: Charles Girault's Petit Palais (1900), now the Musée des Beaux-Arts de la Ville de Paris, redrawn on its real footprint: the building's outline in OpenStreetMap's data (as Overture Maps carries it, simplified to 0.6 m) set in the plot at the museum's point, north up — a trapezoid of four wings round a D-shaped garden court, its 122 m front a few degrees off north-south and facing the avenue Winston-Churchill on the west. The first model laid the front along the north side with no turn and stood on 45% of the plot's building cells; this one stands on 86% and covers all 144 of them (node scripts/fit_ground.js). Read from the Commons photographs of the front (2012, 2015), the north wing, the dome and the aerial photograph of 2018: 16 m of pale limestone walls on a 4.8 m stone plinth, a balustrade, steep flat-topped slate mansards to 22.4 m with stone chimney stacks and glass skylights along their tops, round corner pavilions under slate domes, the great arched porch with its gilded gate and a stair of three flights up to it, behind it the central dome on its drum (36.8 m to the finial), tall first-floor windows about every five metres (drawn as flush glass), single columns every 4.8 m along the front, and the semicircular court with its low roofed peristyle (an arcade of single columns on the garden side), lawns, gravel and two pools. Guessed: every height (no scaled elevation was found; read against the 122 m front and the windows), the peristyle's width, the corner towers' sizes, the pools and trees, the gardens round it, the colonnade's spacing. Not drawn: the sculpture, the urns, the dormers, the ground-floor arches.
